findings.summary: Deleting a row from shop.support_tickets, or changing its key, makes the database look for matching rows in shop.ticket_events (800K rows) without an index, which means reading the whole table. Queries that load ticket_events rows for one support_tickets row can't seek either.
findings.title: ticket_events has no index on ticket_id, its foreign key to support_tickets
verify: Deletes from shop.support_tickets should no longer scan shop.ticket_events; re-scan to confirm the finding is gone.

findings.summary: No query has read ix_orders_status_created in the 1 hours since the server last restarted, while shop.orders was written 0 times. It still has to be updated on every insert, and on updates that touch its columns, and it takes 32.3 MB of storage and buffer memory.
findings.title: ix_orders_status_created on orders is never read

caveats: ix_orders_status is narrower, so scans of it read fewer pages. Keep it if a hot query scans it rather than seeking.

findings.title: ix_orders_status is covered by the wider ix_orders_status_created on orders

fix.sql:
EXEC sp_configure 'show advanced options', 1; RECONFIGURE;
EXEC sp_configure 'cost threshold for parallelism', 50; RECONFIGURE;
fix.summary: A common starting point is 50; adjust with your workload.

findings.summary: Even cheap queries go parallel, which wastes CPU on coordination and shows up as CXPACKET/CXCONSUMER waits.
findings.title: Cost threshold for parallelism is still the 1990s default of 5
